facts.text: Donna Deegan is the 45th mayor of Jacksonville and the ninth since the city's 1968 consolidation; she was sworn in on July 1, 2023.
In May 2023 she became the first woman elected mayor of Jacksonville.
She graduated from Florida State University and worked more than 25 years in broadcast journalism, ending as a lead anchor at First Coast News.
She founded the DONNA Foundation in 2003 to support cancer patients and their families.
She describes herself as a fifth-generation Jacksonville native and a three-time cancer survivor.
She announced in April 2026 that she is seeking a second term.

priorities.text: Infrastructure: roads, parks, drainage and resilience projects.
Public safety: pay increases for police and firefighters, and Jacksonville Journey Forward, a community-led initiative on the root causes of crime.
Streamlining permitting and development processes.
Building more housing, reducing homelessness and investing in under-resourced communities.
Literacy, youth development and recreation programs, and broader access to healthcare.
Downtown investment, including a new University of Florida campus, and regular town halls across the city.

quotes.text: Together, we will build a healthy, safe, resilient, inclusive, and innovative city that works for all of us. Every person will have a voice in City Hall and a seat at the table to reach that goal.
make city government more accessible, restore trust, and ensure that every neighborhood shares in Jacksonville’s growth.

He worked in governmental affairs for the St. Johns River Water Management District, and since 2018 has worked as a political consultant and development manager.
Florida Politics identifies him as a lobbyist for the VyStar Credit Union.

He has served on the boards of the Literacy Alliance of Northeast Florida and the Memorial Park Association, on the Changing Homelessness Continuum of Care, and as a member of the Veterans Council of Duval County.

The city's member page lists him on the Transportation, Energy & Utilities Committee, the Jacksonville Waterways Commission and the Neighborhoods, Community Services, Public Health & Safety Committee, with liaison roles including the Downtown Investment Authority, Downtown Vision and the Homelessness Initiatives Commission.

priorities.text: Says he worked with the Jacksonville Association of Fire Fighters to restore a defined-benefit pension, secure pay raises and fund modern equipment for first responders.
Says he has focused on fighting for the city's oldest neighborhoods and residents who have not seen a Council member in years.
Says roads and potholes are not partisan issues and criticizes bickering and gamesmanship on the City Council.
Supported a 2026 bill to expand the Downtown Business Improvement District and said he was open to discussing amendments with the Jacksonville Jaguars.
In February 2026 called on Council President Kevin Carrico to temporarily step down from the presidency amid questions about his actions regarding a JEA Board position; Carrico rejected the call.

quotes.text: I believe in my last 4 years on Council I’ve demonstrated that willingness to work with everyone to accomplish important goals for our city, while also fighting for our oldest neighborhoods and the residents who haven’t seen a Councilmember in years

However, potholes and roads don’t care what political party you are, and residents are sick of what they are seeing from leadership in City Council. The bickering, gamesmanship and ignoring the needs of our residents hold back the great potential of this City.
Support for public safety can’t be just a political talking point; it’s a tangible record of delivering for our brave first responders
I’m in support of this, but if there’s any amendments or edits, I’m happy to discuss, and I’m happy to discuss this with the Jaguars

facts.text: He is a Jacksonville native who graduated with honors from Raines High School, where he played football.
He holds a Bachelor's degree in Business Administration from Florida A&M University and a Master of Business Administration from the University of Phoenix.
He began his career at the Duval County Clerk of Courts.
He won election to represent District 7 in November 2022 and March 2023, and District 8 in May 2023, after a May 2023 court-ordered redistricting placed him in the new District 8.
District 8 is located mostly north of the Trout River and includes Jacksonville International Airport and the UF Health North hospital.
His current standing committee assignments are the Transportation, Energy & Utilities Committee and the Land Use & Zoning Committee.

priorities.text: His official biography lists changing the stigma surrounding mental health, advocating for others, reducing crime and fostering strategic infrastructure development.
In November 2023 he said his office had worked for months with the City's legal team to address public health and safety issues at Northwood Apartments, and welcomed an emergency injunction there.

facts.text: She is a Jacksonville native and lives in the Woodstock community, where she settled 23 years ago.

She graduated from William M. Raines High School in 1986, earned a Bachelor of Arts from Florida A&M University in 1991, and a master's degree in Education from the University of North Florida in 2009.
She served in the U.S. Army Reserve as a non-commissioned officer, rising to Staff Sergeant before an honorable discharge in 2001.
She has taught middle and high school students in Duval County since 1993.

She joined the Northwest Citizens Planning and Advisory Committee in 2015 and served six years on the North Florida Transportation Planning Organization Citizen Advisory Committee, rising to Vice-Chairman.
She served on the Community Based Crime Reduction Committee for over two years.
On the council she is Vice Chair of the Neighborhoods, Community Investments & Services Committee and a member of the Transportation, Energy & Utilities Committee.

priorities.text: In January 2024 she called a press conference to discuss the City's efforts to restore public safety at the Valencia Way Apartments, which the Public Nuisance Abatement Board had served with a Complaint for Public Nuisance Abatement.
She serves on the Jacksonville Housing & Community Development Commission and the Florida League of Cities, and as an alternate on Military/Veterans Affairs.

facts.text: She is a Jacksonville native and the current City Council member for District 10.
She is President and Chief Executive Officer of the Clara White Mission, where the Mission says she has served for 33 years.
Her current council assignments are Member of the Rules Committee and Vice Chair of the Transportation, Energy & Utilities Committee.
Her special assignments include the Florida Association of Counties, the Transportation Planning Organization (TPO), Sister Cities liaison and alternate member of the Election Canvassing Board.
She served on the transition teams of Jacksonville Mayors John Delaney, John Peyton, Alvin Brown and Lenny Curry.
She is a member of Leadership Jacksonville, Leadership Florida, the Civitans, the Junior League and the Downtown Rotary Club.

She holds an Associate in Arts from Florida State College at Jacksonville and a Bachelor of Science in business administration from Jones College, which also gave her an honorary Doctorate of Humane Letters.

priorities.text: Economic development and revitalization in District 10.
Implementing a larger vision to build on District 10 and its assets.
Collaborating with law enforcement, community and neighborhoods to reduce criminal activities.
At the Clara White Mission she led veteran services, vocational training and job placement, and affordable housing programs.
She has led the development of Eartha's Farm & Market, a 10.5-acre Clara White Mission initiative to expand access to fresh food in food desert communities.

quotes.text: Go out of your comfort zone to make a difference

facts.text: Born in Jacksonville and a westside native; graduated from Paxon Senior High School in 1972.
Worked 32 years with the Jacksonville Fire and Rescue Department, retiring in 2011 as Deputy Director Assistant Fire Chief.
Served as president of the Jacksonville Association of Firefighters from 2002 to 2003.
Member of the Retired Jacksonville Association of Firefighters, Riverside Rotary Club, Wesconnett Masonic Lodge and the Morocco Shrine.
Serves on the City Council's Land Use & Zoning Committee and Finance Committee.
Council liaison to the Jacksonville Fire Museum Advisory Board and the Police & Fire Pension Board of Trustees, and a member of the TPO.

priorities.text: Public safety, including giving law enforcement and the Jacksonville Fire and Rescue Department the tools they need to do their jobs.
Growth of Cecil Field, which his council page says will bring more jobs, restaurants and hotels to the area.

facts.text: He was elected to the Jacksonville City Council in 2019 and represents District 13, which includes Atlantic Beach, Intercoastal West, Jacksonville Beach, Mayport and Neptune Beach.
He is a Captain in the U.S. Army and Florida National Guard, and in 2023 deployed to the Middle East with the 40th Infantry Division as Chief of Military Justice.
He was previously Chief Executive Officer of K9s For Warriors, a provider of service dogs for disabled American veterans.
He was a litigator at two international law firms and served as a Special Assistant United States Attorney for the U.S. Department of Justice.
He founded The FireWatch, a regional effort to combat veteran suicide.
On the council he is Vice Chair of the Land Use & Zoning Committee, a member of the Finance Committee, and liaison for Military/Veterans Affairs and the Jacksonville Transportation Authority.

priorities.text: Advocates for veterans, focusing on combat-related PTSD, traumatic brain injuries, veteran suicide and veteran homelessness.
In 2015 he partnered with then-Rep. Ron DeSantis to author and introduce the PAWS Act, signed into law in 2021.

facts.text: He is a Jacksonville, Florida native.
He earned degrees at Edward Waters University (BA), Seton Hall University (MA) and Jackson State University (Ph.D.).
He was elected to the Jacksonville City Council in 2023 and represents District 14.
His career spans public service, higher education, journalism, media and the arts.
On the council he serves on the Finance and Land Use & Zoning committees, and chairs the Jacksonville Waterways Commission and the Value Adjustment Board.

He represents Jacksonville on the Board of Directors of the Florida League of Cities and is council liaison to the Joint Planning Commission, the Jacksonville Public Library and the Cultural Council of Greater Jacksonville.

He is a member of organizations including Kappa Alpha Psi Fraternity, the Society of Professional Journalists, the National Association of Black Journalists, the United Nations Association of the United States and SAG-AFTRA.
He is the author of the poetry book Living, Loving, Letting Go.

priorities.text: Helped advance the widening of Old Middleburg Road.
Secured inclusion of an annual HBCU game in Jacksonville's Stadium of the Future agreement.
Leads the effort to codify a Neighborhood Bill of Rights.

Championed historical markers and memorials, including a monument to the Sapelo Seven, a memorial to Johnnie Mae Chappell, renaming the Jacksonville Fire Museum for Henry Bradley, and the Ray Charles Place designation.
